# Fitness status — 2026-09-26

Window: 2026-09-13 to 2026-09-26 (14 days)

## Summary

**Training load & consistency.** 11 activities in 14 days: 7 runs (50.4 km, about 7h10m), 2 road rides (93.8 km, about 5h26m) and 2 short walks (4.7 km). Total moving time is about 13.6 h. The second week was a bit bigger than the first: 4 runs for 28.3 km plus a 43 km ride, against 3 runs for 22.0 km plus a 50 km ride. The biggest days were 19-20 Sep, a 50 km ride (TE 3.9) followed by the Mont Bre hill run (113 min, max HR 168, anaerobic TE 1.9, load 138). Most runs were easy aerobic sessions (avg HR 127-135, TE 2.9-3.6), including today's 5.35 km recovery-style run (avg HR 128, TE 3.0). Garmin's status moved from Maintaining to **Productive** on 20 Sep and has stayed there. Acute load is 408 against chronic 348 (ACWR optimal), so the load is ramping gently, not spiking.

**Recovery signals.** Training readiness mostly sat at 55-77. The one dip was **26 (LOW) on 21 Sep**, the day after the ride plus hill-run block, when body battery bottomed at 5 for three days running (19-21 Sep) and the sleep score fell to 53. It rebounded fast: 58 on 22 Sep, a peak of 89 on 24 Sep, and 71 today. Nightly HRV ranged 41-57 and was BALANCED every day. The 7-day average drifted slightly down, from 53 to 47, and has been flat at 47-48 for the past week. Resting HR is stable and low at 49-53 bpm, with a brief 52-53 bump on 20-21 Sep, and has held at 49 for the last four days. Sleep averaged about 7.5 h with scores of 70-91 (91 on both 24 and 25 Sep), apart from the 53 on 21 Sep. Last night was shorter (6.5 h, score 79). Average stress was low at 16-30, except 41-46 on the 19-20 Sep training days. Every endpoint has data for all 14 days.

**VO2max trend.** Per-run readings: 13 Sep 40, 14 Sep 40, 16 Sep 40, 21 Sep 40, 25 Sep 41, 26 Sep 41. The 20 Sep Mont Bre run has no value. That is flat to slightly rising, and a one-point change is within normal noise. The account-level trend (generic) is populated and says the same thing, creeping from 40.3 to 41.0 over the window. There is no cycling VO2max.

**Observations / suggestions.** (1) The 19-20 Sep back-to-back block (ride plus hill run) is the only thing that pushed recovery into the red: readiness 26, body battery at 5, sleep score 53. Recovery took about 2 days, so put an easy day or rest after that kind of pairing, as you did on 22 Sep. (2) Acute load (408) is now about 17% above chronic (348) after runs on consecutive days (25-26 Sep). With last night's shorter sleep (6.5 h), tomorrow is a sensible easy or rest day. (3) The HRV weekly average has settled about 5 ms lower than two weeks ago while still BALANCED. Keep an eye on it, and if it slips below the mid-40s along with a rising resting HR, back off.
